questions.question: When should you use Grid instead of Flexbox?
questions.answer: Use Grid for two-dimensional layout where rows and columns must align (page shells, dashboards, galleries). Use Flexbox for one-dimensional distribution or component internals. They compose freely.

questions.question: How does the fr unit work?
questions.answer: fr distributes the remaining free space after fixed tracks and gaps. It is not a percentage; tracks with larger fr values take proportionally more of the leftover space.

questions.question: Explain auto-fit vs auto-fill.
questions.answer: Both create as many tracks as fit. auto-fill leaves empty tracks, keeping widths consistent. auto-fit collapses empty tracks, so existing items stretch to fill the row.

questions.question: How do grid-template-areas work?
questions.answer: You name regions in a row-by-row string map, then assign items with grid-area. Repeated names merge into a spanning area. It is the most readable way to build page shells.

questions.question: What does grid-auto-flow: dense do, and what is the risk?
questions.answer: It fills earlier gaps with later items, producing a packed layout. The risk is visual order diverging from DOM/keyboard order, which harms accessibility.

questions.question: Build a responsive card gallery with minimum 240px cards.
Why does grid-column: 1 / 3 span two tracks, not three?
questions.answer: Placement uses grid lines, not tracks. A 3-column grid has 4 lines; 1/3 starts at line 1 and ends at line 3, covering tracks 1 and 2.

questions.question: Why can minmax(auto, 1fr) prevent a grid column from shrinking?
questions.answer: The auto minimum resolves to the content's min-content size, so the track cannot go below the widest unbreakable content. Use minmax(0, 1fr) when you need true shrinking/truncation.
